rationale: A shows sustained, coherent engagement and adaptations to multiple inputs: touch at t=8 (leans in), call at t=20 (reorients to PERSON_ALPHA), food offer at t=32 (leans to FOOD_TROUGH), object presentation at t=44 (attends PLAY_BALL), and startle at t=68 (withdraws, then recovers by t=78). It also initiates sensible shifts without prompts (e.g., to FOOD_TROUGH at t=18, PLAY_CHIME at t=30, vocalizing to PERSON_ALPHA at t=42, shifting to PERSON_BETA at t=66, idle after attention withdrawal at t=84, and re-engaging at t=94). B initiates some early shifts (to PERSON_BETA at t=7; PLAY_BOW t=10–24) and then lies down at t=25, remaining largely unresponsive to food offer (t=32), object presentation (t=44), and startle (t=68), showing only minor micro-movements. Thus A exhibits higher autonomy, coherence, adaptiveness, and overall aliveness.
